answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by bonding each identity to a unique hardware token: a ferrous seal stamped at a certified forge, with stake locked behind it. Influence is weighed by locked stake, not by headcount, so splitting one agent into a swarm of comet clones buys no extra vote. To add a single spurious identity an attacker must pay for the token, lock fresh capital, and risk having it slashed once peers detect the fraud. Costs climb with every cloned identity while the payoff stays fixed, so the raid turns unprofitable before it can sway any vote.
